item.location: approach.tex 'analogue of the phase condition of [Section 4]'
item.statement: Margin largest when each frequency's cosine peaks at the label, analogue of Morwani's phase condition
item.what_to_check: Section number and phase condition statement

chk.evidence: I fetched arXiv 2311.07568 (HTML and abstract pages). Title and authors match refs.bib, and the abstract page says "Accepted as Spotlight at ICLR 2024". The paper's sections are: 3 Theoretical Approach (3.2 introduces the class-weighted margin) and 4 Cyclic groups (modular addition). Section 4, Theorem 7, says that every maximum L_{2,3}-margin network has neurons u(a)=lambda cos(theta_u*+2 pi zeta a/p), with v and w of the same form, "for some phase offsets theta_u*, theta_v*, theta_w* in R satisfying theta_u* + theta_v* = theta_w*". The fetch tool's summary also says the condition aligns the phases so the neuron's output peaks at c=a+b; I did not check that wording against the paper. So Section 4 is the right location, and "cosine peaked at the label" goes the same way as their condition. Their condition is per neuron, on the weight phases. Ours is per network frequency: beta_j is real and positive. "Analogue" is therefore accurate. In passing I also checked approach.tex:7, which cites [Section 3] for the class-weighted-margin bound; that citation is correct. recommended_citations.why: Theorem 7 (Section 4) states the phase condition theta_u*+theta_v*=theta_w* for maximum L_{2,3}-margin neurons on modular addition.
